composio.note: Composio has no managed X app for this toolkit, so you must register your own X app, pay for its API usage, and give Composio its Client ID and Secret. Your users then see your app's name on X's consent screen, not Composio's.

verdict.headline: Create an app in console.x.com, turn on OAuth 2.0 as a confidential Web App, buy API credits, and any X user can connect the same day with no review.
verdict.summary: X does not review OAuth apps. Once you accept the Developer Agreement and describe your use case, any X user can authorize your app. The catch is cost and capability: since Feb 2026 the API is pay-per-use, with credits bought upfront and no free tier documented for new developers. Self-serve tiers also no longer allow likes, follows or quote-posts via the API, and replies are only allowed when the original author summoned you. Many 'agent' actions in older toolkits will therefore fail even though the OAuth connection works.
verdict.time_to_production: Same day. No review gate; production use starts once credits are loaded.
verdict.hands_on_effort: 1-3 hours: console setup, credit purchase and spend limits, Composio config, and a consent/disclosure UX that meets the Developer Policy.
verdict.approval_wait: None for OAuth or self-serve pay-per-use. An Enterprise plan is a sales conversation and is only needed above 3M Post reads per monthly billing cycle. Changing your declared use case later requires notifying X and getting approval.
verdict.cost: Pay-per-use credits with no subscription. Published rates: Post read $0.005/resource, user lookup $0.010/resource, DM event read $0.010/resource, Post create $0.015/request, Post create with a URL $0.20/request, DM create $0.015/request, owned reads $0.001/resource. One-time incentive: $20 in credits when you save your first card and make a first purchase, and up to $50 matching your first auto-recharge. These free incentive credits expire 3 months after grant (purchased credits are not stated to expire).

phases.name: Register developer access and app
phases.goal: Have an X developer account and an app with saved credentials

steps.title: Sign in to the Developer Console and accept the Developer Agreement
steps.detail: Go to console.x.com and sign in with the X account that will own the app. Use a team-controlled account, not a personal one. Accept the Developer Agreement and Policy.
steps.agent_help: Open the console URL and summarize the Developer Policy clauses that matter for an agent: consent before posting, consent before automated replies or DMs, a binding use case, and no storing of X passwords.

steps.title: Describe your use case
steps.detail: Complete your profile by describing how you will use the API. This description is binding: you must notify X and get approval before using X content for a substantively different purpose.
steps.agent_help: Draft the use-case text from your product spec. Name the exact actions the agent takes (read timeline, draft and post with user confirmation, read and send DMs on request). State that users approve each post and that you honor opt-outs. You paste and submit it.

steps.title: Create the app and store credentials immediately
steps.detail: Click 'New App' and enter a name, description and use case. The console generates the API Key/Secret, Bearer Token, Access Token/Secret and the OAuth 2.0 Client ID/Secret. Credentials are shown only once; if you lose them, regenerating invalidates the old ones. X recommends separate apps for development, staging and production.
steps.agent_help: Prepare a secrets-manager entry template (X_CLIENT_ID, X_CLIENT_SECRET) so nothing is pasted into chat.

phases.name: Configure OAuth 2.0
phases.goal: Have OAuth 2.0 user authentication enabled with correct client type and callback URLs

steps.title: Enable OAuth 2.0 user authentication as a Web App (confidential client)
steps.detail: In the app's user authentication settings, enable OAuth 2.0 and choose Web App or Automated App/Bot. These are confidential clients and receive a Client Secret, which Composio needs. Native App and Single Page App are public clients that use PKCE only, with no secret. OAuth 2.0 works only with X API v2.
steps.agent_help: Confirm in the docs which app type maps to a confidential client before you click, and tell you to pick 'Web App'.

steps.title: Register callback URLs exactly
steps.detail: Add https://backend.composio.dev/api/v3/toolkits/auth/callback for Composio. For local testing, add http://127.0.0.1:<port>/<path>; X says not to use 'localhost'. Matching is exact, including trailing slashes. Each app allows up to 10 callback URLs, and production URLs must use https.
steps.agent_help: Produce the exact strings to paste, including trailing-slash variants your code actually sends, and check them against the redirect_uri your Composio auth config emits.

steps.title: Copy the OAuth 2.0 Client ID and Client Secret
steps.detail: These are separate from the OAuth 1.0a API Key/Secret. Composio's OAuth2 auth config needs the OAuth 2.0 pair.

phases.name: Fund the app and set spend controls
phases.goal: Have API calls that are billable and bounded

steps.title: Buy credits and save a payment method
steps.detail: Credits are bought upfront in the Developer Console and drawn down per request. Reads are billed per resource returned and writes per request. Saving a first eligible card and making a first purchase earns $20 in free credits.
steps.agent_help: Estimate monthly spend from expected agent actions per user using the published per-endpoint rates.

steps.title: Set a spending limit and decide on auto-recharge
steps.detail: When the per-billing-cycle spending limit is reached, API requests are blocked until the next cycle. Auto-recharge tops up below a threshold you set and needs a default payment method. It runs at most once per 5 minutes.
steps.agent_help: Recommend a cap and a recharge threshold based on the spend estimate, and add alerting for blocked requests in your app.

phases.name: Connect to Composio
phases.goal: Have your own X account connected through your own app via Composio

steps.title: Create a custom auth config for TWITTER in Composio
steps.detail: In Composio, go to Auth Configs, click Create Auth Config, choose the Twitter toolkit, and select OAuth2. Paste your Client ID and Client Secret and click Create, then pass the auth config ID (ac_...) in your session's authConfigs. Use the redirect URI the Composio dashboard shows: https://backend.composio.dev/api/v3/toolkits/auth/callback. Some toolkits still default to the legacy https://backend.composio.dev/api/v1/auth-apps/add, so register whichever URI the dashboard displays, character for character.
steps.agent_help: Create the auth config through the Composio API or SDK once you supply the secret through an env var. Check that the displayed redirect URI exactly matches an X callback URL.

steps.title: Request the right scopes, including offline.access
steps.detail: A typical agent set is tweet.read users.read tweet.write offline.access, plus dm.read/dm.write or media.write if needed. Without offline.access, X issues no refresh token and the connection dies after the 2-hour access token expires.
steps.agent_help: Set the scope list on the auth config and remove scopes for actions your tier cannot perform, such as like.write and follows.write.

steps.title: Connect your own account and smoke-test
steps.detail: Run the Composio connect flow and approve on X. The authorization code must be exchanged within 30 seconds, which Composio handles server-side. Then call GET /2/users/me (75 requests per 15 minutes per user) and, if you plan to post, create one test Post. Each test call is billed.
steps.agent_help: Generate the connect link, then once you approve on X, run the test calls and report the token expiry, granted scopes and any 4xx responses.

phases.name: Launch
phases.goal: Have arbitrary X users connect safely and within policy

steps.title: Ship consent UX that satisfies the Developer Policy
steps.detail: Get express, informed consent before posting, following or changing profiles on a user's behalf; signing in alone is not consent. Show users exactly what will be published. Get explicit consent before automated replies or DMs, and honor opt-outs immediately. Show a privacy policy before sign-up.
steps.agent_help: Implement a confirm-before-post step and an opt-out handler in the agent, and draft privacy-policy language for X data. You approve the final text.

steps.title: Gate agent actions your tier cannot perform
steps.detail: Since Apr 2026, following, likes and quote-posts via the API are removed from all self-serve tiers. Since Feb 2026, programmatic replies via POST /2/tweets are allowed only when the original author summoned the replier. Remove or hide these tools in the agent.
steps.agent_help: Audit the Composio TWITTER tool list you expose and disable like, follow, quote-post and unsolicited-reply tools.

requirements.item: X account plus accepted Developer Agreement and use-case description
requirements.detail: Signed in at console.x.com. The use case is binding, and material changes need X's approval.

requirements.item: Prepaid API credits and a payment method
requirements.detail: The API is pay-per-usage with no subscription. The pricing page describes no free tier beyond the new-user credit incentive.

requirements.item: OAuth 2.0 enabled as a confidential client (Web App or Automated App)
requirements.detail: Needed to get a Client Secret for server-side token exchange through Composio.
Up to 10 per app, with trailing slashes significant. Use https in production and 127.0.0.1 rather than localhost for local development.
The privacy policy must be shown before sign-up. You need express consent before posting or sending automated replies or DMs.
Only needed above 3M Post reads per monthly billing cycle. It goes through an interest form and sales.

scopes.purpose: Read Posts, timelines and search on the user's behalf
scopes.review_impact: No review. Every Post returned is billed at $0.005 per resource.

scopes.purpose: Identify the connected user (GET /2/users/me) and look up profiles
scopes.review_impact: No review. User lookups are billed at $0.010 per resource.

scopes.purpose: Get a refresh token so the agent keeps access beyond the 2-hour access token
scopes.review_impact: No review. Without it, no refresh token is issued.

scopes.purpose: Create and delete Posts on the user's behalf
scopes.review_impact: No review, but policy requires showing users exactly what will be posted and getting consent. Billed at $0.015 per Post, or $0.20 if it contains a URL. Replies only work when the author summoned you.

scopes.purpose: Upload images or video to attach to Posts

scopes.review_impact: No review, but storing DMs requires express consent and DM content must not be served to unauthorized people. Billed at $0.010 per DM event. Rate limit is 15 requests per 15 minutes per user.
No review. Explicit consent is needed before automated DMs. Billed at $0.015 per request, with limits of 15 per 15 minutes and 1,440 per 24 hours per user.
The scopes still exist, but following and likes via the API were removed from all self-serve tiers in Apr 2026. Expect failures unless you are on Enterprise.

scopes.purpose: Read the connected user's email address
scopes.review_impact: No review documented. Email retrieval with OAuth 2.0 became available in Apr 2025.

oauth.pkce: Required. code_challenge and code_challenge_method (S256 or plain) are authorize-URL parameters for the Authorization Code with PKCE flow. Confidential clients also authenticate with Client ID/Secret; public clients use PKCE only and send client_id in the body.
oauth.refresh_tokens: Issued only when the offline.access scope is requested. Refresh with grant_type=refresh_token at the token URL. Access tokens last 2 hours by default. The authorization code expires 30 seconds after approval. Refresh-token lifetime and rotation are not stated on the fetched page.
oauth.redirect_uri_rules: Must exactly match a callback URL registered on the app, trailing slashes included. Up to 10 per app. Use https in production. For local development use http://127.0.0.1, not localhost. javascript:, data:, file:, ftp: and mailto: schemes are disallowed. Wildcards are not documented.

limits.limit: POST /2/tweets: 100 per 15 minutes per user, 10,000 per 24 hours per app
limits.applies_when: All self-serve apps using user tokens

limits.limit: DM reads: 15 per 15 minutes per user. DM sends: 15 per 15 minutes and 1,440 per 24 hours per user.
limits.applies_when: Agents that read or send DMs

limits.limit: 3 million Post reads per monthly billing cycle
limits.how_to_lift: Apply for Enterprise via the interest form linked from the pricing page

limits.limit: Requests blocked when your spending limit or credit balance is exhausted
limits.applies_when: You set a per-cycle spending limit or credits run out
limits.how_to_lift: Raise the limit, top up, or enable auto-recharge (at most once per 5 minutes)

limits.limit: No likes, follows or quote-posts via the API. Replies only when the author summoned you.
limits.applies_when: All self-serve tiers (since Apr 2026 and Feb 2026 respectively)
limits.how_to_lift: Not documented beyond the self-serve vs Enterprise distinction

blockers.symptom: X rejects the authorize request instead of showing consent, for example when 'localhost' is used or a trailing slash differs
blockers.fix: Register the exact redirect_uri Composio sends (https://backend.composio.dev/api/v3/toolkits/auth/callback). For local development use 127.0.0.1.

blockers.symptom: The connection works for about 2 hours, then API calls return 401 and re-auth is needed
blockers.fix: Add offline.access to the auth config scopes and reconnect

blockers.symptom: The app type is Native or Single Page App (a public client), so Composio's OAuth2 config has no secret to use
blockers.fix: Switch user authentication settings to Web App or Automated App (confidential)

blockers.blocker: Credits exhausted or spending cap hit
blockers.symptom: API requests are blocked until the next billing cycle or a top-up
blockers.fix: Top up, raise the cap, or enable auto-recharge, and alert on this state

blockers.blocker: Agent tries to like, follow, quote-post or reply unsolicited
blockers.symptom: The request is rejected even though the OAuth scopes were granted
blockers.fix: Remove those tools from the agent. These actions are not available on self-serve tiers.

blockers.symptom: The Client Secret is no longer viewable in the console
blockers.fix: Regenerate it (which invalidates the old one) and update the Composio auth config

agent_can: Draft the binding use-case description and the privacy-policy section on X data
Generate exact callback URL strings and verify they match Composio's redirect_uri
Create the Composio auth config via API with the right scope list, including offline.access
Run smoke tests (GET /2/users/me, a test Post) after you approve consent, and report scopes and expiry
Estimate monthly API spend from per-endpoint rates and recommend a spending cap
Disable agent tools for actions self-serve tiers no longer allow (like, follow, quote-post, unsolicited replies)
you_must: Sign in to console.x.com with the owning X account and accept the Developer Agreement
Submit the use-case description and create the app
Copy and store the Client ID and Secret (shown once)
Add a payment card, buy credits and set the spending limit
Approve the OAuth consent screen for your own test connection
Notify X and get approval before materially changing your use case

uncertain: Refresh-token lifetime and whether X rotates refresh tokens on each refresh are not stated on the fetched OAuth 2.0 page. Store any new refresh_token returned.

No free tier is documented for new developers. The changelog (Feb 6 2026) says Legacy Free users got a one-time $10 voucher and that 'Basic and Pro plans remain available' for existing subscribers. Third-party and forum summaries say legacy Basic and Pro migrate to pay-per-use after Jun 1 and Sep 1 2026; the forum announcements returned HTTP 403 and could not be verified. The same changelog entry says Public Utility Apps 'continue to receive free scaled access', but no eligibility criteria were found.
X says per-endpoint rates 'are subject to change'. The figures here are from the pricing page as fetched on 2026-10-28.
Whether the OAuth token exchange itself is billed is not documented. GET /2/users/me is a user lookup and probably costs $0.010.
The exact HTTP status and error body returned when credits or the spending limit are exhausted were not found in official docs.
The fetched docs no longer mention the older 'Project' container for apps. Apps are created directly in console.x.com, and it is unclear whether Projects still exist.
The OAuth page's example authorize URL uses scope names (account.follows.read/write) that are not in its scope table. Use the table names.
Time estimates are hands-on estimates, not provider SLAs. There is no review, so no wait time is published.
